summary.headline: Praj Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 231 million (from INR 192 million) on revenue of INR 8.49 billion; order intake weak at INR 7.15 billion.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations was INR 8.49 billion in Q2 FY27 versus INR 8.42 billion a year earlier, with PBT of INR 361 million (INR 296 million) and PAT of INR 231 million (INR 192 million). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 15.6 billion versus INR 14.8 billion, and H1 PAT was INR 347 million versus INR 246.2 million. Order intake fell to INR 7.15 billion in the quarter, and management said Greenfield ethanol projects in India are stalled by customer funding gaps and feedstock restrictions. Management pointed to CBG, international bioenergy, GenX data-centre and precision-fabrication work as the sources of H2 order growth.

segments.name: Bioenergy
segments.commentary: 69% of revenue and 57% of Q2 order intake. Domestic first-generation ethanol orders are mostly brownfield and co-product/feedstock-flexibility upgrades; Greenfield backlog conversion is slowed by customer funding and feedstock restrictions.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: 21% of revenue and 26% of Q2 order intake. Includes GenX (Mangaluru facility approved by 18 international customers, 4 framework agreements operational).

segments.name: PHS
segments.commentary: 10% of revenue and 17% of Q2 order intake. Management describes the conventional ZLD and PHS business as steady, with new demand from batteries, semiconductors and solar cells.

segments.name: GenX (within Engineering)
segments.commentary: Management guided H1 GenX operating expenses of roughly INR 25-30 crore excluding interest and depreciation, about INR 44-45 crore including them. Targets breakeven in about 12 months, requiring turnover of INR 500-600 crore against annual fixed costs of INR 140-150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Order inflow expected to improve in H2 FY27 from three areas: CBG, international ethanol markets, and GenX equipment/modules.
Management says it will meet the previously indicated GenX order inflow range of INR 800-1,000 crore for FY27; revenue timing is less certain and may slip into FY28.

GenX revenue expected to ramp from Q3/Q4 FY27; breakeven targeted within about 12 months, with INR 500-600 crore of turnover needed to cover roughly INR 140-150 crore of annual fixed costs including interest and depreciation.
CBG JV with BPCL (50:50, INR 100 crore each, board in-principle approval): JV set-up in 2-3 months, first plant about 15 months from commercial production, 8-10 plants over 2-3 years.
Management reaffirmed the FY2030 vision of about INR 10,000 crore revenue and ~50% exports, but said inflection points have been delayed.
Bio-IBA plant in India expected to be completed by end-2026; bio-isobutanol demonstration and scale-up targeted for beginning of next year (early 2027).
Ethanol-to-SAF project FID expected in Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: CBG JV with BPCL: INR 100 crore equity from Praj (matched by BPCL); theoretical 8-10 plant programme could need INR 800-1,000 crore total capex over time.

GenX has seven sheds with construction complete; two are equipped with plant, machinery and cranes. Additional sheds need limited incremental equipment rather than major capex, and are variable cost if volumes rise.
GenX facility is held on a 10-year lease; about seven years remain, so interest and depreciation from the lease will persist.
Bio-IBA plant (India's first) under construction, expected completion by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic Greenfield ethanol projects are slowing due to customer funding challenges and ethanol supply-demand imbalance. Projects based on juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses are affected; clarity is expected by end of FY27.
OMCs excluded sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from 2026-27 ethanol tenders, leaving C-heavy molasses, maize and broken rice as permitted feedstock.
International opportunity pipeline of about INR 1,000 crore over the next few quarters (USA, Brazil, Argentina, Southeast Asia, Africa), driven by ethanol blending mandates; this excludes GenX.
GenX data-centre order is an extension from the same hyperscaler customer under a tie-up of about USD 52 million to be delivered over 2.5 years; order value not disclosed due to confidentiality.
Government E100 recognition for flex-fuel vehicles (CMVR amendment) noted as a potential driver of future ethanol capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Can order inflow sustain around the current level and grow 10-15% next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better order bookings in H2 from CBG, international ethanol and GenX equipment/modules, without quantifying growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will GenX approvals translate into orders and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders expected to start trickling in from next quarter; revenue effect seen from Q4 FY27 onwards, with H2 showing a larger ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Have EBITDA margins bottomed at around 6.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed the Q2 margin of about 6.2% is the floor and unlikely to fall below it, with GenX revenue expected to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GenX data-centre order new or an extension, and is FY27 guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: The order is an extension from the same customer under the USD 52 million tie-up. FY27 order booking expected in line with prior indication; revenue timing less certain. Order size not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How much order inflow can the CBG JV generate and what is the time frame?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are shortlisted; 8-10 plants possible at INR 100 crore each from Praj and BPCL, with orders over about the next year. Management did not give a figure for order value.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Praj taking equity in CBG when it has been asset-light?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited government price and offtake guarantees, Praj's press-mud technology track record (about 5,000 tonnes CBG in 500 days), and co-product revenue such as bio-manure and bio-bitumen to improve ROI.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BPCL forming JVs with other companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a single JV has finite capacity and BPCL may want around 50 plants, so it is entering multiple JVs.

qa_highlights.question: What is GenX breakeven and PBT requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said total fixed cost including interest and depreciation is about INR 140-150 crore per year, requiring turnover of INR 500-600 crore for breakeven.

risks_watch: Order intake of INR 7.15 billion is weak and needs H2 conversion of CBG, international and GenX orders to validate the run-rate.
Greenfield ethanol backlog (juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses based) is at risk until customer funding and feedstock issues resolve, with clarity expected by end FY27.
GenX revenue ramp and breakeven depend on delivering INR 500-600 crore turnover within 12 months; the data-centre order value is undisclosed.
CBG JV carries equity exposure and sector history of delays and margin pressure; project economics not yet proven at scale.
Bio-IBA and bio-isobutanol commercialisation depends on diesel blending policy outside management's control; demonstration targeted for early 2027.
FY2030 revenue vision of INR 10,000 crore is maintained but timelines have slipped.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term opportunities (CBG, GenX data centres, international ethanol) but cautious on near-term Greenfield execution and revenue timing. Management repeatedly qualified targets as dependent on order flow and policy outcomes.
key_quotes: We have delivered improved performance over the previous quarter. This is due to disciplined execution, increased volume, and a better mix.
Overall, we believe the business environment is challenging but improving.
It will take time over several years to get to a realization.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: CFO said Q2 EBITDA margin of ~6.2% is the floor and GenX revenue from Q4 FY27 is expected to lift margins, though GenX carries INR 140-150 crore annual fixed costs including interest and depreciation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: GenX Mangaluru has seven sheds with construction complete and two equipped; additional sheds need limited incremental equipment, and Bio-IBA plant completion is expected by end-2026, so capacity comes live without major capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 order intake fell to INR 7.15bn and revenue rose only ~0.8% (INR 8.49bn vs 8.42bn); H2 recovery depends on CBG, international ethanol and GenX orders, with Greenfield ethanol stalled by customer funding and feedstock restrictions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board has in-principle approved a 50:50 CBG JV with BPCL at INR 100 crore each, with JV set-up in 2-3 months and a theoretical 8-10 plant programme needing INR 800-1,000 crore total capex; ethanol-to-SAF FID is expected Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantified revenue or margin upgrade; H1 PAT grew to INR 347m from INR 246.2m but order intake fell to INR 7.15bn and GenX breakeven was stretched to 12 months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: GenX revenue timing may slip into FY28 and Greenfield ethanol backlog is at risk until customer funding and feedstock clarity by end FY27; FY2030 INR 10,000 crore vision timelines already slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bio-isobutanol demonstration and scale-up targeted for early 2027 after Bio-IBA plant completion by end-2026, though it depends on diesel blending policy.

rows.label: International ethanol pipeline (~INR 1,000 crore)
rows.why: Pipeline of about INR 1,000 crore across USA, Brazil, Argentina, SE Asia and Africa driven by blending mandates, but international share is already 38% of Q2 order intake of INR 7.15bn and conversion not quantified.

rows.label: GenX FY27 order inflow INR 800-1,000 crore
rows.why: Management says it will meet the INR 800-1,000 crore GenX order range for FY27 and orders start trickling in next quarter, though the USD 52m data-centre tie-up value is undisclosed.

rows.label: GenX breakeven within ~12 months
rows.why: Breakeven needs INR 500-600 crore turnover against INR 140-150 crore annual fixed costs; the target was pushed out to about 12 months, so this is conditional on the ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident on CBG, GenX data-centre orders, international ethanol and the CFO's 6.2% margin floor, but cautious on Greenfield ethanol execution, GenX revenue timing and FY2030 timelines; analysts probed order growth, GenX revenue timing and CBG order flow.
